html:
The Ta'an Kwäch'än are a First Nation of the southern Yukon, Canada, whose land centres on Lake Laberge and the Yukon River just north of Whitehorse. They speak Southern Tutchone and are close to the neighbouring Kwanlin Dün and Champagne and Aishihik peoples. They lived by fishing, hunting caribou and moose, and trading with the coastal Tlingit.

The Klondike Gold Rush of 1896 to 1899 sent thousands of gold seekers down the Yukon through Lake Laberge, and the town of Whitehorse grew up on their land. Their council signed a land claim and self-government agreement with Canada and the Yukon in 2002.
